title: Allow me to introduce you, to Hotel Marieux!
author: mushroomsarefriends
selftext: Basically the idea is that Claude and me are building a hotel that will be used for a horror game setting. The player works as a security guard and has to explore the hotel during his night shift, finding disturbing things as he does. I could never have built an entire hotel on my own without generative AI, but with gen AI it's possible. Claude builds the hotel and I check whether it looks good.

comments.author: Top_Issue_7032
comments.body: Looks fantastic! well done. Makes me want to give it a try. Did you make it all in one shot or did you work with your agent some to get it to that level of detail?

replies.author: mushroomsarefriends
replies.body: Thanks! It was actually a lot of back-and-forth between me and Claude.

comments.author: TheKaleKing
comments.body: Really cool. What framework/engine do you use to make it if any?

replies.author: mushroomsarefriends
replies.body: Thanks! The 3d models are all procedurally made by code in these screenshots, but I later added two NPCs that I generated with other AI generators online. I tried having Claude generate a 3d model originally, but that's really not a success because Claude has no visual feedback loop.

replies.author: TheKaleKing
replies.body:
Nice so claude code made all the models in these screenshots? Or was it another AI that created the code for the model and then you had claude integrate it?

I use Meshy for 3d models it's pretty sweet. The low-poly though isn't that great yet but still decent. You can get something pretty great at like 8k-10k poly. Chatgpt image to model in there works surprisingly well.

replies.author: mushroomsarefriends
replies.body: Yeah Claude made everything in these screenshots. I use Meshy for 3d models too, throwing in a suitable chatGPT generated image and having Meshy turn it into a model.

replies.author: TheKaleKing
replies.body: Nice, thanks for sharing. And in this screenshot is that rendered in some sort of engine like Unity or something?

replies.author: mushroomsarefriends
replies.body: Yes, the whole project is made in Unity.
